summary: Tsutomu Kubo (1883–1972) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo under Raphael von Koeber and later earned a doctorate from Tohoku University. He held academic posts at Tokyo, Tohoku University, and Toyo University.
Tsutomu Yamaguchi (born 1953) works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Hokkaido University and was attested as a collaborative researcher at the Eastern Institute in 2015.

Tsuyoshi Yokoyama works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He pursued doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2015–2017) and served as a project researcher at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, attested in 2017.

Tu Weiming (born 1940) specializes in philosophy, Sinology, and religious studies. Educated at Tunghai, Tokai, and Harvard universities under scholars including Zongsan Mou, he held faculty posts at Princeton, UC Berkeley, Harvard, and Peking University.
Tubten Chokyi Dorje (1872–1935) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye, Patrul Rinpoche, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Tubten Gyeltsen Ozer was a scholar who studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Tubten Nyendrak (1883–1959) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Khenpo Shenga.
Tubten Nyima was a scholar who studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.
Tubten Tsondru studied under Dilgo Khyentse, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, and Khenpo Gangshar.
Tukaram Ramchandra Laddu was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Halle until 1912 and held a post at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, attested in 1920.
Tulku Hungkar Dorje is a scholar who studied under Penor Rinpoche and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.

Tulku Sherdor (born 1961) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Vassar College, Naropa University, and the University of Virginia, learning under Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche and Jeffrey Hopkins.

Tulku Thondup (1939–2023) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Dodrupchen Monastery under Kyala Khenpo, Khenpo Chemchok, and Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and served as a visiting scholar at Harvard University.

Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche (1920–1996) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. He studied under Samten Gyatso, Dilgo Khyentse, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Karsé Kongtrul, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and founded Tergar Osel Ling Monastery.

Turrell V. Wylie (1927–1984) worked in Tibetology, Sinology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Washington and under Giuseppe Tucci and Dezhung Rinpoche, later serving as associate professor and professor at the University of Washington.
Tutob Chökyi Wangchuk was a scholar who studied under Dilgo Khyentse, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Trulshik Rinpoche.
Tuyet Tam Thi Pham is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned an MA at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the supervision of Somboon Vuddhikaro and Sanu Mahatthanadull.
Tyler Dewar works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Nitartha Institute and under Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche and Acharya Tashi Wangchuk.

Tzung-Kuen Wen is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Queensland under Primož Pecenko, Tamara Ditrich, and Chris Kang. He also served as a lecturer at Fuyan Buddhist Institute in 2005.
U Ba Khin (1899–1971) was a figure in Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Saya Thetgyi. He founded the International Meditation Centre.
